content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: 8:2 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:2 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

segments.t: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

content.latin: 8:2 Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.
content.english: 8:2 For thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens.

segments.t: Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.

content.latin: 8:3 Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.
content.english: 8:3 Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, * that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.

segments.t: Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.

content.latin: 8:4 Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.
content.english: 8:4 For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: * the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.

segments.t: Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.

content.latin: 8:5 Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?
content.english: 8:5 What is man that thou art mindful of him? * or the son of man that thou visitest him?

segments.t: Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?

content.latin: 8:6 Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
content.english: 8:6 Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * and hast set him over the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.

content.latin: 8:8 Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.
content.english: 8:8 Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, * all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.

segments.t: Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.

content.latin: 8:9 Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.

content.latin: 18:2 Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum eius annúntiat firmaméntum.
content.english: 18:2 The heavens shew forth the glory of God, * and the firmament declareth the work of his hands.

content.latin: 18:3 Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.

segments.t: Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.

segments.t: Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.

content.latin: 18:5 In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

segments.t: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

content.english: 18:6 Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way: * his going out is from the end of heaven,

segments.t: Et occúrsus eius usque ad summum eius: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre eius.

segments.t: Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.

content.english: 18:9 The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: * the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes.

segments.t: Iustítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.

content.english: 18:10 The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: * the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.

segments.t: Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * iudícia Dómini vera, iustificáta in semetípsa.

content.latin: 18:11 Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.
content.english: 18:11 More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: * and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.

segments.t: Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.

content.latin: 18:12 Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.

segments.t: Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.

content.latin: 18:13 Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
content.english: 18:13 Who can understand sins? from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord: * and from those of others spare thy servant.

segments.t: Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.

content.latin: 18:14 Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.

content.latin: 23:1 Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.

content.latin: 23:2 Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
content.english: 23:2 For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

segments.t: Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.

content.latin: 23:3 Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?
content.english: 23:3 Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: * or who shall stand in his holy place?

segments.t: Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?

content.latin: 23:4 Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec iurávit in dolo próximo suo.
content.english: 23:4 The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, * who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.

segments.t: Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec iurávit in dolo próximo suo.

content.latin: 23:5 Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
content.english: 23:5 He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, * and mercy from God his Saviour.

segments.t: Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.

content.latin: 23:6 Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.
content.english: 23:6 This is the generation of them that seek him, * of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

segments.t: Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.

content.latin: 23:7 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:7 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

segments.t: Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: 23:8 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.
content.english: 23:8 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.

segments.t: Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.

content.latin: 23:9 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:9 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

segments.t: Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: 23:10 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:10 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory.

segments.t: Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Péperit Fílium suum primogénitum, et reclinávit eum in præsépio.
content.english: Ant. She brought forth her first-born Son, and laid Him in a manger.

segments.t: Ant.
Péperit Fílium suum primogénitum, et reclinávit eum in præsépio.

content.latin: ℣. Sancta Dei Génetrix, semper Virgo María.
content.english: ℣. Holy Mother of God, Mary, always a Virgin,

segments.t: Sancta Dei Génetrix, semper Virgo María.

content.latin: ℟. Intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum.
content.english: ℟. Pray for us, unto the Lord our God.

segments.t: Intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

segments.t: Benedictio.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: De Libro Ecclesiástici
content.english: Lesson from the book of Ecclesiasticus

content.latin: 11 In ómnibus réquiem quæsívi, et in hereditáte Dómini morábor.
content.english: 11 And by my power I have trodden under my feet the hearts of all the high and low: and in all these I sought rest, and I shall abide in the inheritance of the Lord.

segments.t: In ómnibus réquiem quæsívi, et in hereditáte Dómini morábor.

content.latin: 12 Tunc præcépit, et dixit mihi Creátor ómnium: et, qui creávit me, requiévit in tabernáculo meo,
content.english: 12 Then the creator of all things commanded, and said to me: and he that made me, rested in my tabernacle,

segments.t: Tunc præcépit, et dixit mihi Creátor ómnium: et, qui creávit me, requiévit in tabernáculo meo,

content.latin: 13 Et dixit mihi: In Iacob inhábita, et in Israël hereditáre, et in eléctis meis mitte radíces.
content.english: 13 And he said to me: Let thy dwelling be in Jacob, and thy inheritance in Israel, and take root in my elect.

segments.t: Et dixit mihi: In Iacob inhábita, et in Israël hereditáre, et in eléctis meis mitte radíces.

content.latin: 14 Ab inítio et ante sǽcula creáta sum, et usque ad futúrum sǽculum non désinam, et in habitatióne sancta coram ipso ministrávi.
content.english: 14 From the beginning, and before the world, was I created, and unto the world to come I shall not cease to be, and in the holy dwelling place I have ministered before him.

segments.t: Ab inítio et ante sǽcula creáta sum, et usque ad futúrum sǽculum non désinam, et in habitatióne sancta coram ipso ministrávi.

content.latin: 15 Et sic in Sion firmáta sum, et in civitáte sanctificáta simíliter requiévi, et in Ierúsalem potéstas mea.
content.english: 15 And so was I established in Sion, and in the holy city likewise I rested, and my power was in Jerusalem.

segments.t: Et sic in Sion firmáta sum, et in civitáte sanctificáta simíliter requiévi, et in Ierúsalem potéstas mea.

content.latin: 16 Et radicávi in pópulo honorificáto, et in parte Dei mei heréditas illíus, et in plenitúdine sanctórum deténtio mea.
content.english: 16 And I took root in an honourable people, and in the portion of my God his inheritance, and my abode is in the full assembly of saints.

segments.t: Et radicávi in pópulo honorificáto, et in parte Dei mei heréditas illíus, et in plenitúdine sanctórum deténtio mea.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Súmite psaltérium iucúndum in insígni die solemnitátis vestræ:
content.english: ℟. Take the pleasant harp, in the time appointed, on your solemn feastday;

segments.t: Súmite psaltérium iucúndum in insígni die solemnitátis vestræ:

content.latin: * Et exsultáte Vírgini adiutríci nostræ.
content.english: * And sing aloud unto the Virgin our strength.

content.latin: ℣. Cantáte ei cánticum novum: annuntiáte inter gentes glóriam eius.
content.english: ℣. O sing unto her a new song, declare her glory among the heathen.

segments.t: Cantáte ei cánticum novum: annuntiáte inter gentes glóriam eius.

content.latin: ℟. Et exsultáte Vírgini adiutríci nostræ.
content.english: ℟. And sing aloud unto the Virgin our strength.

segments.t: Et exsultáte Vírgini adiutríci nostræ.

content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 17 Quasi cedrus exaltáta sum in Líbano, et quasi cypréssus in monte Sion:
content.english: 17 I was exalted like a cedar in Libanus, and as a cypress tree on mount Sion.

segments.t: Quasi cedrus exaltáta sum in Líbano, et quasi cypréssus in monte Sion:

content.latin: 18 Quasi palma exaltáta sum in Cades, et quasi plantátio rosæ in Iericho:
content.english: 18 I was exalted like a palm tree in Cades, and as a rose plant in Jericho:

segments.t: Quasi palma exaltáta sum in Cades, et quasi plantátio rosæ in Iericho:

content.latin: 19 Quasi olíva speciósa in campis, et quasi plátanus exaltáta sum iuxta aquam in platéis.
content.english: 19 As a fair olive tree in the plains, and as a plane tree by the water in the streets, was I exalted.

segments.t: Quasi olíva speciósa in campis, et quasi plátanus exaltáta sum iuxta aquam in platéis.

content.latin: 20 Sicut cinnamómum et bálsamum aromatízans odórem dedi: quasi myrrha elécta, dedi suavitátem odóris;
content.english: 20 I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon. and aromatical balm: I yielded a sweet odour like the best myrrh:

segments.t: Sicut cinnamómum et bálsamum aromatízans odórem dedi: quasi myrrha elécta, dedi suavitátem odóris;

content.latin: 21 Et quasi storax, et gálbanus, et úngula, et gutta, et quasi Líbanus non incísus vaporávi habitatiónem meam, et quasi bálsamum non mixtum odor meus.
content.english: 21 And I perfumed my dwelling as storax, and galbanum, and onyx, and aloes, and as the frankincense not cut, and my odour is as the purest balm.

segments.t: Et quasi storax, et gálbanus, et úngula, et gutta, et quasi Líbanus non incísus vaporávi habitatiónem meam, et quasi bálsamum non mixtum odor meus.

content.latin: 22 Ego quasi terebínthus exténdi ramos meos, et rami mei honóris et grátiæ.
content.english: 22 I have stretched out my branches as the turpentine tree, and my branches are of honour and grace.

segments.t: Ego quasi terebínthus exténdi ramos meos, et rami mei honóris et grátiæ.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Vidi speciósam ascendéntem désuper rivos aquárum; cuius inæstimábilis odor erat nimis;
content.english: ℟. I saw the fair one going up above the rivers of waters, a priceless savour hung heavy;

segments.t: Vidi speciósam ascendéntem désuper rivos aquárum; cuius inæstimábilis odor erat nimis;

content.latin: * Et sicut dies verni circúmdabant eam flores rosárum et lília convállium.
content.english: * And about her it was as the flower of roses in the spring of the year, and lilies of the valleys.

content.latin: ℣. Astitit Regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto, circúmdata varietáte.
content.english: ℣. Upon thy right hand did stand the Queen in a vesture of gold, wrought about with diverse colours.

segments.t: Astitit Regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto, circúmdata varietáte.

content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 24 Ego mater pulchræ dilectiónis, et timóris, et agnitiónis, et sanctæ spei.
content.english: 24 I am the mother of fair love, and of fear, and of knowledge, and of holy hope.

segments.t: Ego mater pulchræ dilectiónis, et timóris, et agnitiónis, et sanctæ spei.

content.latin: 25 In me grátia omnis viæ et veritátis, in me omnis spes vitæ et virtútis.
content.english: 25 In me is all grace of the way and of the truth, in me is all hope of life and of virtue.

segments.t: In me grátia omnis viæ et veritátis, in me omnis spes vitæ et virtútis.

content.latin: 26 Transíte ad me, omnes qui concupíscitis me, et a generatiónibus meis implémini;
content.english: 26 Come over to me, all ye that desire me, and be filled with my fruits.

segments.t: Transíte ad me, omnes qui concupíscitis me, et a generatiónibus meis implémini;

content.latin: 27 Spíritus enim meus super mel dulcis, et heréditas mea super mel et favum.
content.english: 27 For my spirit is sweet above honey, and my inheritance above honey and the honeycomb.

segments.t: Spíritus enim meus super mel dulcis, et heréditas mea super mel et favum.

content.latin: 28 Memória mea in generatiónes sæculórum.
content.english: 28 My memory is unto everlasting generations.

segments.t: Memória mea in generatiónes sæculórum.

content.latin: 29 Qui edunt me, adhuc esúrient, et qui bíbunt me, adhuc sítient.
content.english: 29 They that eat me, shall yet hunger: and they that drink me, shall yet thirst.

segments.t: Qui edunt me, adhuc esúrient, et qui bíbunt me, adhuc sítient.

content.latin: 30 Qui audit me non confundétur, et qui operántur in me non peccábunt.
content.english: 30 He that hearkeneth to me, shall not be confounded: and they that work by me, shall not sin.

segments.t: Qui audit me non confundétur, et qui operántur in me non peccábunt.

content.latin: 31 Qui elúcidant me, vitam ætérnam habébunt.
content.english: 31 They that explain me shall have life everlasting.

segments.t: Qui elúcidant me, vitam ætérnam habébunt.

content.english: Psalm 44 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 44

content.latin: 44:2 Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
content.english: 44:2 My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

segments.t: Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.

content.latin: 44:2 Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: 44:2 My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

segments.t: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.

content.latin: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

segments.t: Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.

content.latin: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
content.english: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

segments.t: Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.

content.latin: 44:5 Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: 44:5 With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

segments.t: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

content.latin: 44:5 Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
content.english: 44:5 Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

segments.t: Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.

content.latin: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
content.english: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

segments.t: Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.

content.latin: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
content.english: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

segments.t: Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.

content.latin: 44:8 Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
content.english: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

segments.t: Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.

content.latin: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
content.english: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

segments.t: Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.

content.latin: 44:10 Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.

content.latin: Cum Albigénsium hǽresis per Tolosátium regiónem ímpie grassarétur, atque áltius in dies radíces ágeret, sanctus Domínicus, qui nuper Prædicatórum órdinis fundaménta iécerat, ad eam convelléndam totus incúbuit. Id ut præstáret valídius, auxílium beátæ Vírginis, cuius dígnitas illis erróribus impudentíssime petebátur, cuíque datum est cunctas hǽreses interímere in univérso mundo, eníxis précibus implorávit. A qua (ut memóriæ próditum est) cum mónitus esset ut Rosárium pópulis prædicáret, velut singuláre advérsus hǽreses ac vítia præsídium; mirum est quanto mentis fervóre et quam felíci succéssu iniúnctum sibi munus sit exsecútus. Est autem Rosárium certa precándi fórmula, qua quíndecim angelicárum salutatiónum décades, oratióne Domínica interiécta, distínguimus, et ad eárum síngulas tótidem nostræ reparatiónis mystéria, pia meditatióne recólimus. Ex eo ergo témpore pius hic orándi modus mirabíliter per sanctum Domínicum promulgári augeríque cœpit. Quem eiúsdem institutórem auctorémque fuísse, summi Pontífices apostólicis lítteris passim affirmárunt.
content.english: When the heresy of the Albigenses was making head against God in the County of Toulouse, and striking deeper roots every day, the holy Dominic, who had but just laid the foundations of the Order of Friars Preachers, threw his whole strength into the travail of plucking these blasphemies up. That he might be fitter for the work, he cried for help with his whole soul to that Blessed Maiden, whose glory the falsehoods of the heretics so insolently assailed, and to whom it hath been granted to trample down every heresy throughout the whole earth. It is said that he had from her a word, bidding him preach up the saying of the Rosary among the people, as a strong help against heresy and sin, and it is wonderful with how stout an heart and how good a success he did the work laid upon him. This Rose-garden (or Rosary) is a certain form of prayer, wherein we say one-hundred-and-fifty times the salutation of the Angel, and the Lord's Prayer between every ten times, and, each of the fifteen times that we say the Lord's Prayer, and repeat tenfold the salutation, think of one of fifteen great events in the history of our Redemption. From that time forth this form of godly prayer was extraordinarily spread about by holy Dominic, and waxed common. That this same Dominic was the founder and prime mover thereof hath been said by Popes in diverse letters of the Apostolic See.

content.latin: Innumerábiles porro fructus ex hac tam salutári institutióne in christiánam rempúblicam dimanárunt. Inter quos victória illa mérito numerátur, quam sanctíssimus Póntifex Pius quintus et ab eo inflammáti christiáni príncipes apud Echínadas ínsulas de Turcárum tyránno potentíssimo reportárunt. Nam, cum illa ipsa die ea victória reláta sit, qua die sacratíssimi Rosárii sodalitátes per univérsum orbem consuétas supplicatiónes perágerent statutásque preces de more fúnderent, iis précibus haud immérito refértur accépta. Quod quidem cum étiam Gregórius tértius décimus testátus esset; ut pro tam singulári benefício beátæ Vírgini sub appellatióne Rosárii perénnes grátiæ ubíque terrárum haberéntur, in ecclésiis ómnibus, in quibus altáre Rosárii foret, Offícium, ritu dúplici maióri, perpétuo de eo celebrándum indíxit; aliíque Pontífices Rosárium recitántibus eiusdémque Rosárii sodalitátibus indulgéntias pene innúmeras concessére.
content.english: From this healthy exercise have grown up numberless good fruits in the Christian Commonwealth. Among these deserveth well to be named that great victory over the Sultan of Turkey, which the most holy Pope Pius V, and the Christian Princes whom he had roused, won at Lepanto, (on the 7th day of October, the first Lord's Day in the month, in the year of our Lord 1571) The day whereon this victory was gained was the very one whereon the Guildbrethren of the most holy Rosary, throughout the whole world, were used to offer their accustomed prayers and appointed supplications, and the event therefore was not unnaturally connected therewith. This being the avowed opinion of Gregory XIII, he ordered that in all Churches where there was, or should be, an Altar of the Rosary, a Feast, in the form of a Greater Double, should be kept for ever upon the first Lord's Day of the month of October, to give unceasing thanks to the Blessed Virgin, under her style of (Queen of) the (Most Holy) Rosary, for that extraordinary mercy of God. Other Popes also have granted almost numberless Indulgences to those who say the Rosary, and to those who join its Guilds.

content.latin: Clemens vero undécimus, ánimo réputans insígnem páriter victóriam, anno millésimo septingentésimo décimo sexto in Hungáriæ regno a Cárolo sexto in imperatórem Romanórum elécto de innúmeris Turcárum cópiis relátam, eo die contigísse quo festum Dedicatiónis sanctæ Maríæ ad Nives celebrarétur, atque eódem ferme témpore quo sacratíssimi Rosárii confrátres públicam solemnémque supplicatiónem in alma Urbe, ingénti pópuli concúrsu magnáque religióne, peragéntes, férvidas ad Deum preces pro Turcárum depressióne fúnderent ac poténtem opem Deíparæ Vírginis in auxílium Christianórum humíliter implorárent; eam ob rem, victóriam illam, nec non liberátam paulo post eorúndem Turcárum obsidióne Corcyrénsem ínsulam, eiúsdem beátæ Vírginis patrocínio pie cénsuit adscribéndam. Quam ob rem ut huius quoque tam insígnis benefícii perénnis semper et memória exstáret et grátia, sacratíssimi Rosárii festum eódem ritu celebrándum ad Ecclésiam univérsam exténdit. Hæc ómnia Benedíctus décimus tértius in Breviário Románo appóni iussit. Leo autem tértius décimus in turbulentíssimis Ecclésiæ tempóribus, diúque preméntium malórum sæva tempestáte, cunctos in orbe fidéles, iterátis apostólicis lítteris ad Mariális Rosárii, præsértim per octóbrem mensem, frequéntiam veheménter incéndit, aucto quoque ánnui festi solemnitátis ritu, additáque litaníis Lauretánis Regínæ sacratíssimi Rosárii invocatióne, et Offício de eádem solemnitáte próprio Ecclésiæ univérsæ concésso. Sanctíssimam ergo Dei Genetrícem cultu hoc eídem gratíssimo iúgiter venerémur; ut, quæ tóties Christi fidélibus, Rosárii précibus exoráta, terrénos hostes profligáre dedit ac pérdere, inférnos páriter superáre concédat.
content.english: In the year 1716, Charles VI, Elect-Emperor of the Romans, won a famous victory over countless hordes of Turks, near Timisoara, in the kingdom of Hungary, upon the day when the Feast of the Dedication of the Church of St. Mary of the Snows was being kept, and almost at the very moment when the Guild-brethren of the most holy Rosary were moving through the streets of Rome in public and solemn procession, amid vast multitudes, all filled with the deepest enthusiasm, calling vehemently upon God for the defeat of the Turks, and entreating the Virgin Mother of God to bring the might of her succour to the help of the Christians. A few days later, (upon the Octave of the Feast of the Assumption,) the Turks raised the siege of Corfu. These mercies Clement XI devoutly ascribed to the helpful prayers of the Blessed Virgin, and that the memory and the sweetness of such a blessing might for all time coming endure gloriously, he extended to the whole Church the observance of the Feast of the most holy Rosary, for the same day and of the same rank, (as it had already been in the places before mentioned.) Benedict XIII commanded the record of all these things to be given a place in the Service-book of the Church of Rome; and Leo XIII, in the most troublous times of the Church and the cruel storm of long pressing evils, by fresh Apostolic letters vehemently urged upon all the faithful throughout the earth the often saying of the Rosary of (the Blessed Virgin) Mary, raised the dignity of the yearly festival, added to the Litany of Loretto the Invocation Queen of the Most Holy Rosary, and granted to the whole Church a special Office for this solemn occasion. Let us all then be earnest in honouring the most holy Mother of God in this form which she liketh so well, that even as the entreaties of Christ's faithful people, approaching her in her Garden of Roses, have so often won her to scatter and destroy their earthly foes, so she may gain for them the victory over their hellish foes likewise.

content.latin: In illo témpore: Missus est Angelus Gábriel a Deo in civitátem Galilǽæ, cui nomen Názareth, ad Vírginem desponsátam viro, cui nomen erat Ioseph, de domo David, et nomen Vírginis María. Et réliqua.
content.english: At that time the angel Gabriel was sent from God into a city of Galilee, called Nazareth, to a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary. And so on.

content.latin: Ad commendatiónem grátiæ suæ et ad destructiónem humánæ sapiéntiæ, Deus de fémina sed vírgine dignátus est carnem assúmere, ut símilem símili rédderet, contrárium contrário curáret, pestíferam spinam evélleret, peccáti chirógraphum potentíssime deléret. Heva spina fuit; María rosa éxstitit. Heva spina, vulnerándo; María rosa, ómnium afféctus mulcéndo. Heva spina, infígens ómnibus mortem; María rosa, reddens salutíferam ómnibus sortem. María rosa fuit cándida per virginitátem, rubicúnda per caritátem; cándida carne, rubicúnda mente; cándida virtútem sectándo, rubicúnda vítia calcándo; cándida afféctum purificándo, rubicúnda carnem mortificándo; cándida Deum diligéndo, rubicúnda próximo compatiéndo.
content.english: To commend His Own love towards us, and to bring to nought the wisdom of men, God was pleased to take flesh of a woman, albeit a virgin, that He might bring like against like, heal by opposites, pluck out the poisonous thorn, and blot out mightily the handwriting of our sin that was against us. Eve was a thorn, Mary is a rose. Eve is a thorn that pierceth, Mary is a rose that charmeth all the senses. Eve was a thorn that fixed death into all, Mary is a rose that bringeth health to all. Mary was a white rose through her virginity, and a red rose through her love. She was white in her flesh, red in her mind; white in that she followed the path of grace, red in that she trod down sin; white by the purity of her affections, red by the mortification of her body; white by her love for God, red by her compassion for her neighbour.

content.latin: Verbum caro factum est, et hábitat iam in nobis. Hábitat in memória nostra, hábitat in cogitatióne, quia usque ad ipsam descéndit imaginatiónem. Quonam modo, inquis? Nimírum iacens in præsépio, in virgináli grémio cubans, in monte prǽdicans, in oratióne pernóctans, in cruce pendens, in morte pallens, liber inter mórtuos et in inférno ímperans, seu étiam tértia die resúrgens, et Apóstolis loca clavórum, victóriæ signa, demónstrans, novíssime coram eis cæli secréta conscéndens. Quid horum non vere, non pie, non sancte cogitátur?
content.english: The Word was made flesh, and dwelleth even now among us. He dwelleth in our memory. He dwelleth in our thought. He hath come down even unto our imagination; and how sayest thou doth he so? By lying in the manger, by nestling in His mother's breast, by preaching upon the mountain, by remaining all night in prayer to God, by hanging upon the Cross, by turning pale in death, by going down free among the dead and triumphing in hell, by rising again the third day, by showing to the Apostles the places of the nails the marks of his victory, by ascending up into heaven while they all beheld Him, of which of these things think we not with truth, with godliness, with holiness?

content.latin: Quidquid horum cógito, Deum cógito; et per ómnia est Deus meus. Hæc ego meditári dixi sapiéntiam, et prudéntiam iudicávi eructáre memóriam suavitátis; quóniam in huiuscémodi núcleis virga sacerdotális copiósa prodúxit, quam, in supérnis háuriens, ubérius nobis María refúdit. In supérnis plane et ultra Angelos, quæ Verbum ex ipso Patris corde suscépit.
content.english: If I think of any of these, I think of God, and He is my God through them all. To think of these things I have decreed to be wisdom, and to set forth the memory of their sweetness I have judged to be prudence. The rod of Aaron the Priest brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds; but these things are the almonds of that Rod which came forth out of the stem of Jesse, the Rod whereof sprang the flower, a Rod which was raised in Mary into places higher than the earthly tabernacle, higher indeed, even into places higher than angels, since she received the Word into herself out of the very heart of the Eternal Father.

content.latin: 62:2 Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
content.english: 62:2 O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.

segments.t: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.

content.latin: 62:2 Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
content.english: 62:2 For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

segments.t: Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.

content.latin: 62:3 In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
content.english: 62:3 In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.

segments.t: In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.

content.latin: 62:4 Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
content.english: 62:4 For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.

segments.t: Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.

content.latin: 62:5 Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
content.english: 62:5 Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.

segments.t: Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.

content.latin: 62:6 Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
content.english: 62:6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

segments.t: Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.

content.latin: 62:7 Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.
content.english: 62:7 If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.

segments.t: Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.

content.latin: 62:8 Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
content.english: 62:8 And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.

segments.t: Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.

content.latin: 62:10 Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
content.english: 62:10 But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

segments.t: Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.

content.latin: 62:12 Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
content.english: 62:12 But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

segments.t: Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Spíritus Dómini replévit orbem terrárum.
content.english: Ant. The spirit of the Lord hath filled the world.

segments.t: Ant.
Spíritus Dómini replévit orbem terrárum.

content.latin: Ant. Assúmpta est * María in cælum: gaudent Angeli, laudántes benedícunt Dóminum, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Mary hath been taken to heaven. * The angels rejoice; they praise and bless the Lord. Alleluia.

segments.t: Ant.
Assúmpta est * María in cælum: gaudent Angeli, laudántes benedícunt Dóminum, allelúia.

content.latin: Canticum Trium Puerorum [4]
content.english: Canticle of the Three Young Men [4]

segments.t: Canticum Trium Puerorum

content.latin: 3:57 Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:57 All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:58 Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:58 O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:

segments.t: Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:59 Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:61 Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:62 Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:68 Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:69 Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:70 Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:71 Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:73 Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.
content.english: 3:73 O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:74 Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:74 O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless ye the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:) Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:75 (Bow head) Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost; * let us praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:)
Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:56 Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:56 Blessed art thou, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.

segments.t: Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.

content.latin: Ant. Assúmpta est María in cælum: gaudent Angeli, laudántes benedícunt Dóminum, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Mary hath been taken to heaven. The angels rejoice; they praise and bless the Lord. Alleluia.

segments.t: Ant.
Assúmpta est María in cælum: gaudent Angeli, laudántes benedícunt Dóminum, allelúia.

content.latin: Ant. Exaltáta est * Virgo María super choros Angelórum, et in cápite eius coróna stellárum duódecim.
content.english: Ant. The Virgin Mary * hath been exalted over choirs of angels, and upon her head there is a crown of twelve stars.

segments.t: Ant.
Exaltáta est * Virgo María super choros Angelórum, et in cápite eius coróna stellárum duódecim.

content.latin: Psalmus 148 [5]
content.english: Psalm 148 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 148

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

segments.t: Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

segments.t: Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

segments.t: Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

segments.t: Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

segments.t: Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:

content.latin: 148:11 Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.
content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

segments.t: Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.

content.latin: 148:12 Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.
content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

segments.t: Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
content.english: 148:14 The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

segments.t: Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.

content.latin: 148:14 Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.
content.english: 148:14 A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching him.

segments.t: Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Exaltáta est Virgo María super choros Angelórum, et in cápite eius coróna stellárum duódecim.
content.english: Ant. The Virgin Mary hath been exalted over choirs of angels, and upon her head there is a crown of twelve stars.

segments.t: Ant.
Exaltáta est Virgo María super choros Angelórum, et in cápite eius coróna stellárum duódecim.

content.latin: In me grátia omnis viæ et veritátis, in me omnis spes vitæ et virtútis. Ego, quasi rosa plantáta super rivos aquárum, fructificávi.
content.english: In me is all grace of the way and of the truth; in me is all hope of life and virtue; I have flowered forth like a rose planted by the brooks of water.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: Hymnus
content.english: Hymn

segments.t: Hymnus

content.latin: Iam morte, victor, óbruta,
content.english: Now Christ, the conqueror of death,

content.latin: Ab ínferis Christus redit,
content.english: Breaks sin's enslaving chain,

content.latin: Fractísque culpæ vínculis,
content.english: And rising from the tomb returns,

content.latin: Cæli reclúdit límina.
content.english: And opens heaven again.

content.latin: Visus satis mortálibus
content.english: Awhile beheld by mortal men,

content.latin: Ascéndit ad cæléstia,
content.english: He rises from their sight;

content.latin: Dextrǽque Patris ássidet
content.english: Ascending to the Father's throne,

content.latin: Consors patérnæ glóriæ.
content.english: He reigns in equal light.

content.latin: Quem iam suis promíserat,
content.english: His promised gift unto his own

content.latin: Sanctum datúrus Spíritum,
content.english: He sends forth from above,

content.latin: Linguis amóris ígneis
content.english: And rains the Holy Spirit down

content.latin: Mæstis alúmnis ímpluit.
content.english: In fiery tongues of love.

content.latin: Solúta carnis póndere
content.english: The Virgin, freed of mortal weight,

content.latin: Ad astra Virgo tóllitur,
content.english: Is borne than stars yet higher,

content.latin: Excépta cæli iúbilo
content.english: And with glad melody is hailed

content.latin: Et Angelórum cánticis.
content.english: By each angelic choir.

content.latin: Bis sena cingunt sídera
content.english: Our Mother's gentle brow now shines

content.latin: Almæ paréntis vérticem:
content.english: With crown in starry sheen,

content.latin: Throno propínqua Fílii
content.english: As nigh her Son, in light enthroned,

content.latin: Cunctis creátis ímperat.
content.english: She reigns creation's Queen.

content.latin: Iesu, tibi sit glória,
content.english: O Jesu, born of Virgin bright,

content.latin: Qui natus es de Vírgine,
content.english: All glory be to thee,

content.latin: Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
content.english: With Father and with Paraclete,

content.latin: In sempitérna sǽcula.
content.english: Through all eternity.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Elégit eam Deus, et præelégit eam.
content.english: ℣. God hath chosen her and forechosen her,

segments.t: Elégit eam Deus, et præelégit eam.

content.latin: ℟. Et habitáre eam fecit in tabernáculo suo.
content.english: ℟. And hath made her to dwell in His tabernacle.

segments.t: Et habitáre eam fecit in tabernáculo suo.

content.latin: Ant. Solemnitátem hodiérnam * sacratíssimi Rosárii Genetrícis Dei Maríæ devóte celebrémus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercédat ad Dóminum Iesum Christum.
content.english: Ant. Let us this day keep * right heartily the solemn Feast of the Most Holy Rosary of Mary the Mother of God, that she may pray for us to our Lord Jesus Christ.

segments.t: Ant.
Solemnitátem hodiérnam * sacratíssimi Rosárii Genetrícis Dei Maríæ devóte celebrémus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercédat ad Dóminum Iesum Christum.

content.latin: Canticum Zachariæ
content.english: Canticle of Zacharias

segments.t: Canticum Zachariæ

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

segments.t: Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

segments.t: Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

segments.t: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

segments.t: Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

segments.t: Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

segments.t: Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

segments.t: Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

segments.t: In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

segments.t: Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

segments.t: Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

segments.t: Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

segments.t: Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, cuius Unigénitus per vitam, mortem et resurrectiónem suam nobis salútis ætérnæ prǽmia comparávit: concéde, quǽsumus; ut hæc mystéria sacratíssimo beátæ Maríæ Vírginis Rosário recoléntes, et imitémur quod cóntinent, et quod promíttunt, assequámur.
content.english: O God, Whose only-begotten Son, by His life, death and resurrection, has merited for us the grace of eternal salvation, grant, we beseech You, that, meditating upon those mysteries in the most holy Rosary of the Blessed Virgin Mary, we may imitate what they contain and obtain what they promise.

content.latin: Per eúndem Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: Iam lucis orto sídere,
content.english: Now in the sun's new dawning ray,

content.latin: Deum precémur súpplices,
content.english: Lowly of heart, our God we pray

content.latin: Ut in diúrnis áctibus
content.english: That he from harm may keep us free

content.latin: Nos servet a nocéntibus.
content.english: In all the deeds this day shall see.

content.latin: Linguam refrénans témperet,
content.english: May fear of him our tongues restrain,

content.latin: Ne litis horror ínsonet:
content.english: Lest strife unguarded speech should stain:

content.latin: Visum fovéndo cóntegat,
content.english: His favouring care our guardian be,

content.latin: Ne vanitátes háuriat.
content.english: Lest our eyes feed on vanity.

content.latin: Sint pura cordis íntima,
content.english: May every heart be pure from sin

content.latin: Absístat et vecórdia;
content.english: And folly find no place therein:

content.latin: Carnis terat supérbiam
content.english: Scant need of food, excess denied,

content.latin: Potus cibíque párcitas.
content.english: Wear down in us the body's pride.

content.latin: Ut, cum dies abscésserit,
content.english: That when the light of day is gone,

content.latin: Noctémque sors redúxerit,
content.english: And night in course shall follow on.

content.latin: Mundi per abstinéntiam
content.english: We, free from cares the world affords,

content.latin: Ipsi canámus glóriam.
content.english: May chant the praise that is our Lord's.

content.latin: Deo Patri sit glória,
content.english: All laud to God the Father be,

content.latin: Eiúsque soli Fílio,
content.english: All praise, Eternal Son, to thee:

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
content.english: All glory, as is ever meet,

content.latin: Nunc et per omne sǽculum.
content.english: To God the holy Paraclete.

content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Psalmus 25 [1]
content.english: Psalm 25 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 25

content.latin: 25:1 Iúdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.
content.english: 25:1 Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence: * and I have put my trust in the Lord, and shall not be weakened.

segments.t: Iúdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.

content.latin: 25:2 Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.
content.english: 25:2 Prove me, O Lord, and try me; * burn my reins and my heart.

segments.t: Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.

content.latin: 25:3 Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.
content.english: 25:3 For thy mercy is before my eyes; * and I am well pleased with thy truth.

segments.t: Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.

content.latin: 25:4 Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.
content.english: 25:4 I have not sat with the council of vanity: * neither will I go in with the doers of unjust things.

segments.t: Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.

content.latin: 25:5 Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.
content.english: 25:5 I have hated the assembly of the malignant; * and with the wicked I will not sit.

segments.t: Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.

content.latin: 25:6 Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:
content.english: 25:6 I will wash my hands among the innocent; * and will compass thy altar, O Lord:

segments.t: Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:

content.latin: 25:7 Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.
content.english: 25:7 That I may hear the voice of thy praise: * and tell of all thy wondrous works.

segments.t: Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.

content.latin: 25:8 Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.
content.english: 25:8 I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of thy house; * and the place where thy glory dwelleth.

segments.t: Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.

content.latin: 25:9 Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:
content.english: 25:9 Take not away my soul, O God, with the wicked: * nor my life with bloody men:

segments.t: Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:

content.latin: 25:10 In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.
content.english: 25:10 In whose hands are iniquities: * their right hand is filled with gifts.

segments.t: In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.

content.latin: 25:11 Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * rédime me, et miserére mei.
content.english: 25:11 But as for me, I have walked in my innocence: * redeem me, and have mercy on me.

segments.t: Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * rédime me, et miserére mei.

content.latin: 25:12 Pes meus stetit in dirécto: * in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.
content.english: 25:12 My foot hath stood in the direct way: * in the churches I will bless thee, O Lord.

segments.t: Pes meus stetit in dirécto: * in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.

content.latin: Psalmus 51 [2]
content.english: Psalm 51 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 51

content.latin: 51:3 Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?
content.english: 51:3 Why dost thou glory in malice, * thou that art mighty in iniquity?

segments.t: Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?

content.latin: 51:4 Tota die iniustítiam cogitávit lingua tua: * sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.
content.english: 51:4 All the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice: * as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit.

segments.t: Tota die iniustítiam cogitávit lingua tua: * sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.

content.latin: 51:5 Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem: * iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.
content.english: 51:5 Thou hast loved malice more than goodness: * and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness.

segments.t: Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem: * iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.

content.latin: 51:6 Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, * lingua dolósa.
content.english: 51:6 Thou hast loved all the words of ruin, * O deceitful tongue.

segments.t: Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, * lingua dolósa.

content.latin: 51:7 Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem, * evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo: et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.
content.english: 51:7 Therefore will God destroy thee for ever: * he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living.

segments.t: Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem, * evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo: et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.

content.latin: 51:8 Vidébunt iusti, et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt, et dicent: * Ecce homo, qui non pósuit Deum adiutórem suum:
content.english: 51:8 The just shall see and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say: * Behold the man that made not God his helper:

segments.t: Vidébunt iusti, et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt, et dicent: * Ecce homo, qui non pósuit Deum adiutórem suum:

content.latin: 51:9 Sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum: * et præváluit in vanitáte sua.
content.english: 51:9 But trusted in the abundance of his riches: * and prevailed in his vanity.

segments.t: Sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum: * et præváluit in vanitáte sua.

content.latin: 51:10 Ego autem, sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei, * sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum: et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 51:10 But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, * have hoped in the mercy of God for ever, yea for ever and ever.

segments.t: Ego autem, sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei, * sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum: et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: 51:11 Confitébor tibi in sǽculum, quia fecísti: * et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.
content.english: 51:11 I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: * and I will wait on thy name, for it is good in the sight of thy saints.

segments.t: Confitébor tibi in sǽculum, quia fecísti: * et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.

content.latin: Psalmus 52 [3]
content.english: Psalm 52 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 52

content.latin: 52:1 Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * Non est Deus.
content.english: 52:1 The fool said in his heart: * There is no God.

segments.t: Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * Non est Deus.

content.latin: 52:2 Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.
content.english: 52:2 They are corrupted, and become abominable in iniquities: * there is none that doth good.

segments.t: Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.

content.latin: 52:3 Deus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum: * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.
content.english: 52:3 God looked down from heaven on the children of men: * to see if there were any that did understand, or did seek God.

segments.t: Deus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum: * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.

content.latin: 52:4 Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
content.english: 52:4 All have gone aside, they are become unprofitable together, * there is none that doth good, no not one.

segments.t: Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.

content.latin: 52:5 Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?
content.english: 52:5 Shall not all the workers of iniquity know, * who eat up my people as they eat bread?

segments.t: Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?

content.latin: 52:6 Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.
content.english: 52:6 They have not called upon God: * there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear.

segments.t: Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.

content.latin: 52:6 Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa eórum qui homínibus placent: * confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos.
content.english: 52:6 For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men: * they have been confounded, because God hath despised them.

segments.t: Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa eórum qui homínibus placent: * confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos.

content.latin: 52:7 Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Iacob, et lætábitur Israël.
content.english: 52:7 Who will give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? * when God shall bring back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.

segments.t: Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Iacob, et lætábitur Israël.

content.english: 54:7 And I said: Who will give me wings like a dove, * and I will fly and be at rest?
